# Answer: `generator-shortcuts`

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

## Strongest plausible rival

`first_rectangle_only`: identify aligned rectangle components, apply the canonical partner-colored 3×3 expansion and color-5 guides to the first component, and ignore every later rectangle.

This rival fits **all four canonical demonstrations and the canonical test pair (5/5)**. Every canonical pair contains one rectangle, so “process all rectangles” and “process only the first rectangle” are observationally identical there.

## How the output was checked

I executed the pinned Racket authority through:

```text
python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 0832c700ffb9 \
  --input ../checks/shortcut-witness/input.json \
  --out ../checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json
```

The receipt is `checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json`; it records executed rule hash `781d2d53fe4d`, matching the catalog, input hash `60571e2698ba76be289d7d54dfd2979dd5fede08ab35e05f7d042f81a1d17573`, and output hash `5357b274445a6e332b46cac768af57e876b813e14d8cc767013d75daa2de04bc`. The focused regression `tests/test_review_shortcut_counterexample.py` replays the generator call, checks `self_check`, verifies both hashes, and asserts the 44-cell disagreement.

## Does the generator emit such cases?

**Yes.** This is a normal `two_rects` production draw, not a hand-crafted out-of-domain probe. The ordinary period-three lesson schedule includes `two_rects` twice in every six-pair lesson, so every five-demonstration holdout retains a witness against this shortcut. The 300-lesson census found no surviving declared rival in any production lesson or any of 1,800 query rotations. That finite result refutes the declared shortcut on the tested sampler; it is not a proof against every conceivable rival.
